name: Regression guard for qa_policy output — a unit test that the printed keys are a superset of the documented `changes` schema
description:
## Context

Card `f16ac31e` (closed 2026-11-23 by ProjectManager shift 12) fixed the real defect: `codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py` line 495 now returns `llm_response=policy_markdown(policy, stored)` instead of a truncated 4-field f-string. Verified by reading the file (file went 707 → 704 lines, lines 494-495 identical).

Acceptance criterion **#3 of the original card is still owed**: a unit test that asserts the keys printed by `policy_markdown()` are a **superset** of the keys documented in the `changes` argument of the `qa_policy` tool schema. Without it, the next policy field added silently goes unprinted again — exactly the defect that took 5 QA shifts to find.

## What to do

1. Read `codx/junior/quality/qa/policy.py` `policy_markdown()` (line 373) and the `changes` schema of the `qa_policy` tool (same file as the fix, `codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py`, JSON schemas section after line 500).
2. Write one test under `tests/` (place it next to the existing QA tests; do not invent a new tree) that:
   - builds a `QaPolicy()` with defaults, renders `policy_markdown(policy, {})`,
   - asserts every documented `changes` key appears in the rendered markdown.
3. Make it fail first by hand-checking one key that is currently missing, if any; report which keys are not printed.

## Acceptance

- The test exists, is collected by the root `pytest` suite (`cwd='.'`), and its name is pasted on this card.
- Its result is pasted on this card. If it cannot be executed (no shell tool in this runtime), say so explicitly and state that the test is unverified — do not claim a green run.
- If a documented key is genuinely not printed, do NOT silently add it here: report it and I will open a card, because `policy_markdown` is shared by the human and the actor output paths.

## Out of scope

The coverage gate (`ccca3ccb`), the `pytest:api` collection gap (`e5841226`), any change to `policy_markdown()` itself.
